name: Telefónica building & Plaça de Catalunya (May Days 1937)
story: On 3 May 1937 Catalan police under Eusebio Rodríguez Salas tried to take the Telefónica exchange from the CNT workers' committee that had run it since July 1936. The anarchists opened fire, and within hours barricades went up across Barcelona. The CNT and POUM faced the Generalitat, the PSUC communists and the Republican government forces in the 'May Days'. The PSUC headquarters were at the Hotel Colón across the square. After a ceasefire and the arrival of Assault Guards from Valencia, the government took control of public order in Catalonia. The events led to the suppression of the POUM and the kidnapping and murder of Andreu Nin.
see: The Telefónica building (1926–28) still faces the square, though its dome was removed in 1949; the Hotel Colón stood on the Passeig de Gràcia corner and was later replaced.
plan: Free, always visible; combine with the Poliorama and Rambla stop (5 minutes' walk).

boxes.text: Deaths in the May Days: contemporary press reported about 500 killed; recent research puts it at about 218–235 in Barcelona.
